newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China criticises Manila airstrip on Spratlys.
newsitem.headline: China criticises Manila airstrip on Spratlys.

text.p: China on Monday criticised the Philippines for opening an airstrip on one of the disputed Spratly islands and said Manila should refrain from any act that could harm relations.
"China enjoys indisputable sovereignty over the Nansha (Spratly) Islands and the adjacent water," the Chinese Embassy said in a statement received by Reuters on Monday.
Hao Yinpiao, spokesman for the embassy in Manila, told Reuters that Manila should "refrain from any move to harm" relations.
"What we are hoping for is that both sides should abide by the principles the state leaders have reached," he added.
The Spratlys, a cluster of potentially oil-rich but largely uninhabited islands, shoals and reefs, are claimed wholly or in part by China, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.

Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Philippine President Fidel Ramos agreed during Jiang's visit to Manila last month to shelve differences over the islands and consider cooperation in developing the area.

Tensions between the two countries flared last year after China built structures on one of the islands which Manila said could be used as naval support facilities. Beijing says the buildings are shelters for fishermen.
Hao said no official protest had been lodged with Manila about the inauguration of the airstrip in the Spratlys' Kalayaan group on December 25.
Manila claims ownership of the eight Kalayaan islands.
